original_question: Find an example of a nontrivial graph cocycle action on a Poisson bracket, meaning an action that produces a family of inequivalent Poisson structures not related by a coordinate change.
target_in_paper: Section 1, Introduction: the nearest target is the paper's standard deformation-theory question for Kontsevich's tetrahedral cocycle γ3—whether the γ3-flow on a Poisson bivector is nontrivial—together with footnote 1, which restates this as the open problem of finding an example of nontrivial graph-cocycle action on a Poisson bracket. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already gets the core point right: it asks for an existence example, and it correctly interprets “nontrivial” as meaning “not removable by a coordinate change,” hence giving genuinely inequivalent Poisson structures rather than a reparametrization of the same one. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's immediate cocycle is the tetrahedral cocycle γ3, not an unspecified neighboring cocycle. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The ambient setting is finite-dimensional real affine Poisson geometry, concretely R^d in the nearby discussion, rather than an arbitrary abstract Poisson space. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
The deformed object is a Poisson bivector P, and the relevant infinitesimal action is written as the γ3-flow Ṗ = Q_{γ3}(P^{⊗4}). ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
The paper formulates triviality in terms of a coordinate change generated by a vector field X on R^d. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

An explicit equivalent formulation nearby is cohomological: one asks whether Q_{γ3}(P^{⊗4}) is or is not a Poisson coboundary of the form [[P, X]]. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The “family of inequivalent Poisson structures” should be understood as the one-parameter first-order deformation coming from that infinitesimal flow, not an arbitrary unrelated family; this is an inference from the paper's infinitesimal-flow setup. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

The quantifiers should be explicit: one seeks some dimension d and some Poisson bivector P for which the cocycle action is genuinely nontrivial. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))

No homogeneity, polynomial-degree, nilpotency, or positive-characteristic assumptions belong to this targeted statement; adding them would move away from the paper's actual formulation. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
refined_question: Does there exist a dimension d and a Poisson bivector P on the real affine space R^d such that Kontsevich's tetrahedral cocycle γ3 induces a genuinely nontrivial infinitesimal deformation Ṗ = Q_{γ3}(P^{⊗4}), in the sense that there is no vector field X on R^d with Q_{γ3}(P^{⊗4}) = [[P, X]]; equivalently, the first-order family P_t = P + t Q_{γ3}(P^{⊗4}) + O(t^2) is not obtained from P by a coordinate change and therefore yields inequivalent Poisson structures? ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: Find a Poisson bivector P on some R^d for which the tetrahedral cocycle term Q_{γ3}(P^{⊗4}) is not a Poisson coboundary, i.e. cannot be written as [[P, X]] for any vector field X on R^d. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
justification: The draft is closest to the introduction, not to the later Nambu-specific bulleted problems on page 95. Footnote 1 almost literally matches your wording, but the surrounding introductory sentences make clear that the paper formalizes the issue through the tetrahedral γ3-flow and asks whether that infinitesimal deformation is only a coordinate change along a vector field. The nearby discussion after Eq. (2) gives the corresponding coboundary formulation [[P, X]]. By contrast, the later bulleted open problems concern how to construct trivializing fields X_{d+1}^{γ3} inside the Nambu-determinant setting via descendants and vanishing micro-graphs, which is a different and narrower question. So the refined version fixes γ3, states the Poisson-bivector flow explicitly, and makes the coordinate-change/coboundary criterion precise without drifting into those later recursive-construction problems. ([bjp-bg.com](https://www.bjp-bg.com/papers/bjp2025_s1_090-095.pdf))
